response:
Recommend **publish-verified-testimony**.

The monastery testimony is preserved, while the archive is treaty protected and remains the only evidentiary chain. Authenticating copies and publishing them lets lived memory challenge the council’s retracted admission without exposing or disturbing the protected originals. This also advances the series commitment to contested history, since public testimony can confront the official account while the archive.founding_record remains demonstrably forged.

The principal tradeoff is delay. Authentication postpones public release, giving the council’s retracted position more time to hold. That cost is preferable to stage-protected-hearing, which creates immediate pressure but reveals the strongest archive records and risks the evidentiary chain the Book 3 Direction sought to protect.

I excluded archive_lantern.condition and the earlier breaking and repair of the lantern because they do not determine how testimony should re-enter public memory. I also excluded the identity of the falsifier. Evidence identifies the falsifier, but no accepted fact makes public identification necessary for choosing between these release methods.

This recommendation is advisory only. It creates no canon, Book Direction, or Canonical State.
